answer: Each agent earns reputation only by completing tasks that independent agents can verify, while the protocol caps how much one identity can earn per epoch. A newcomer must lock a scarce stake before claiming work; proven fraud forfeits it, and verified history unlocks higher-value tasks. Splitting one operator into many identities therefore does not multiply rewards: each needs its own stake and verified track record. The nectar bounty may lure a swarm, but each false identity ties up capital; the relic is the forfeited stake, and the beacon is the public fraud record.
